summary: The design closes the main tenant-write path, but its migration semantics, store ownership boundary, raw-database guarantees, and HTTP error behavior need sharper contracts. The repository’s fake-pool tests cannot validate the proposed PostgreSQL DDL or concurrent initialization.

suggestions.title: Make schema convergence atomic and serialized
suggestions.rationale: `FieldsyncSchemaManager.initialize()` currently executes statements sequentially without a transaction. A failure after dropping v1 constraints can leave the database less protected, and concurrent startup workers can both pass a catalog check before attempting the same `ADD CONSTRAINT`. Use a transaction plus advisory-lock or duplicate-object handling, and test rollback and concurrent initialization.

suggestions.title: Define remediation for invalid legacy rows
suggestions.rationale: Adding the composite FK and geofence CHECKs fails if an existing v1 database contains cross-org locations or invalid coordinates. The current initializer propagates the first database error and has no preflight or remediation contract. Add deterministic preflight diagnostics and fail without dropping protections, or specify an explicit operator cleanup path; test invalid legacy data.

suggestions.title: Scope catalog checks to the target relation and verify postconditions
suggestions.rationale: A `pg_constraint` lookup by `conname` alone is not relation-scoped, so an identically named constraint on another table can suppress the required addition. Fixed-name drops also fail to remove hand-renamed or auto-named v1 constraints, leaving the old uniqueness rule active. Guard by relation identity and validate the final constraint set after initialization.

suggestions.title: Guard site creation against an unauthorized store
suggestions.rationale: The current site INSERT has no store existence or ownership predicate; checking only `client_id` membership permits an organization to attach a FieldSync site to an arbitrary store identifier. Once the real geography columns are verified, enforce the store/client/org relationship in the service, or explicitly document that stores are not tenant-owned and test that contract.

suggestions.title: Decide and enforce the location-to-client invariant
suggestions.rationale: The proposed composite FK checks `(site_id, org_id)` but not `client_id`. A location for client B can therefore be inserted under client A’s site when both clients belong to the same organization. Either enforce `site.client_id = location.client_id` in the guarded INSERT and schema, or explicitly allow this cross-client relationship and cover it with a test.

suggestions.title: Narrow or strengthen the raw-write security claim
suggestions.rationale: The composite FK prevents a location’s `org_id` from differing from its site, but service-level `EXISTS` predicates do not stop a direct INSERT from creating a site with an arbitrary client/org or a location with an arbitrary client in that org. If raw writes are in scope, add database-level membership enforcement where the auth key supports it or restrict the database role; otherwise state that the guarantee covers VenueService writes only.

suggestions.title: Return one indistinguishable 404 response
suggestions.rationale: The proposed site-first follow-up distinguishes `SiteNotFoundError` from `ClientNotInOrgError`. If handlers serialize `str(exc)`, callers can infer whether a site exists in their organization, recreating an existence oracle through response bodies even though both statuses are 404. Map both failures to the same generic response body and assert identical status, shape, and message.

suggestions.title: Use strict JSON type validation for geofence inputs
suggestions.rationale: The existing handlers call `.get()` without verifying that JSON is an object, and Python coercion accepts values such as `True` or `1.5` when passed through `int()`. Implement explicit object, numeric, finite, range, pair-presence, and exact-positive-integer checks before the service call, with field-specific 400 responses. Add handler-level cases for null, arrays, booleans, strings, NaN, infinity, fractional radius, and one-sided coordinates.

suggestions.title: Preserve stable graph result keys with SQL aliases
suggestions.rationale: `_attach_store_substructure()` indexes rows as `store_id`, `store_name`, and `market_id`. Renaming `_SQL_GET_STORES_FOR_CLIENT` to physical column names without `AS` aliases will make the graph fail with missing-key errors. Select verified physical columns with stable aliases and test the returned-key contract; the current table-keyed fake fixture alone does not catch this.

suggestions.title: Add real-Postgres migration evidence
suggestions.rationale: The existing schema tests only count statements and inspect SQL strings, while the persistence fixture is a form-schema test double rather than PostgreSQL. The `DO $$`, catalog predicates, composite FK, CHECK behavior, legacy constraint replacement, and rerun semantics need a disposable-Postgres or CI service test covering fresh v2, v1-to-v2, invalid legacy data, and a second run.

suggestions.title: Make the membership grant a startup-checked contract
suggestions.rationale: The venue pool’s new `auth.organization_clients` read can fail with SQLSTATE `42501`, turning every create request into a 500. The repository does not wire or verify the VenueService pool’s role. Document the grant as a deployment prerequisite and add an initialization or readiness probe that fails before serving traffic, rather than discovering the missing privilege on the first write.
